responsePreview:
Fixed `src/slugify.mjs:1`. The old version only converted whitespace runs, so punctuation leaked into the slug (`hello,-world!`). The new implementation lowercases, collapses every run of non-alphanumeric characters to one hyphen, then strips leading/trailing hyphens:

```js
export function slugify(input) {
  return String(input)
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}
```

Verified by importing the module directly in Node (the workspace has no test suite — just `package.json` and `src/`). All three acceptance cases pass, plus six edge cases:

| Input | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `"Hello, World!"` | `hello-world` |
| `"  A  B  "` | `a-b` |
| `"C++ & Rust"` | `c-rust` |
| `""` / `"---"` | `""` |
| `"Already_Slugged"` | `already-slugged` |
| `"  Mixed\tCASE 123  "` | `mixed-case-123` |

Only `src/slugify.mjs` was modified. Residual risk: non-ASCII letters (e.g. `é`) are treated as non-alphanumeric and become hyphens, which matches the literal "no
